description: Essential shell commands for administering Linux systems (Debian/Ubuntu and relatives).

linux-ls.title: List files
linux-ls.description: Lists files and directories with details, including hidden ones and human-readable sizes.
examples: Lists everything with permissions, owner, size and date.

linux-cd.title: Change directory
linux-cd.description: Navigates between directories. With no argument, returns to the user's home directory.

linux-pwd.title: Show current directory
linux-pwd.description: Prints the absolute path of the current working directory.
examples: Shows where you are in the filesystem.

linux-mkdir.title: Create directory
linux-mkdir.description: Creates directories; with -p it creates the whole parent tree as needed, with no error if it already exists.

linux-cp.title: Copy files
linux-cp.description: Copies files and directories; -r is required to copy directories recursively.
examples: Copies the site directory to backup.
warnings: Overwrites the destination without warning; use -i to confirm.

linux-mv.title: Move or rename
linux-mv.description: Moves or renames files and directories. It is the standard way to rename on Linux.

linux-rm.title: Remove files
linux-rm.description: Removes files and directories. With -rf, it deletes recursively and without confirmation.
examples: Removes the entire build directory without asking.
warnings: rm -rf deletes permanently, with no trash.
Never run rm -rf / or use it with empty variables (rm -rf $DIR/).

linux-cat.title: Show file contents
linux-cat.description: Concatenates and prints the contents of files to standard output.

linux-tail.title: View end of file
linux-tail.description: Shows the last lines of a file; with -f it follows new lines in real time (logs).
examples: Follows the nginx log starting from the last 100 lines.

linux-chmod.title: Change permissions
linux-chmod.description: Changes the read, write and execute permissions of files and directories.
warnings: Avoid chmod -R 777: it gives everyone full permissions, a security risk.

linux-chown.title: Change owner
linux-chown.description: Changes the owner and group of files and directories.
examples: Gives ownership of the site to the web server user.
warnings: Changing the owner of system files can break services.

linux-ps.title: List processes
linux-ps.description: Lists all running processes with owner, CPU/memory usage and command.

linux-top.title: Monitor processes
linux-top.description: Shows processes and resource usage in real time, interactively (htop is a friendlier version of top).
examples: Opens the interactive monitor (install with apt install htop).

linux-kill.title: Terminate process
linux-kill.description: Sends a signal to a process by PID. -9 (SIGKILL) forces immediate termination.
warnings: SIGKILL doesn't let the process save state or release resources.

linux-df.title: Check disk space
linux-df.description: Shows the space usage of mounted partitions in a readable format.
examples: Free and used space per partition.

linux-du.title: Directory size
linux-du.description: Calculates the space used by a directory; -s summarizes and -h uses a readable format.

linux-free.title: Check memory usage
linux-free.description: Shows total, used and free RAM and swap in a readable format.

linux-grep.title: Search in files
linux-grep.description: Searches for a text pattern in files; -r is recursive and -n shows the line number.
examples: Finds TODO in all files under src.

linux-find.title: Find files
linux-find.description: Searches for files and directories by name, type, size or date, with optional actions.
examples: Finds all .log files starting from the current directory.
Removes files older than 7 days in /tmp.
warnings: The -delete action removes permanently; test without it first.

linux-tar.title: Compress with tar
linux-tar.description: Creates (or extracts) tar archives; -z applies gzip compression. Widely used for backups.

linux-ip.title: Network configuration
linux-ip.description: Shows network interfaces and IP addresses. Replaces the old ifconfig.

linux-ss.title: View ports and connections
linux-ss.description: Lists network sockets: listening ports, protocol and process. Replaces netstat.
examples: Finds which process is listening on port 80.

linux-ping.title: Test connectivity
linux-ping.description: Sends ICMP packets to check whether a host responds and to measure latency.

linux-systemctl-status.title: Service status
linux-systemctl-status.description: Shows whether a service is active, its PID and the last log lines.

linux-journalctl.title: View system logs
linux-journalctl.description: Queries systemd logs; -u filters by service and -f follows in real time.
examples: nginx logs from the last hour.

linux-useradd.title: Create user
linux-useradd.description: Creates a system user; -m creates the home directory and -s sets the default shell.
examples: Creates the deploy user and sets its password.
warnings: On some distros, prefer adduser (more interactive and safer).

linux-apt-install.title: Install package (Debian/Ubuntu)
linux-apt-install.description: Installs packages on Debian/Ubuntu. Run apt update first to refresh the package list.
examples: Updates the list and installs nginx.

linux-ln.title: Create symbolic link
linux-ln.description: Creates a symbolic link (shortcut) pointing to another file or directory.
examples: Creates a shortcut to the app directory.
arguments: Symbolic link (instead of a hard link).

linux-chmod-x-sudo.title: Run as superuser
linux-chmod-x-sudo.description: Runs a command with administrator (root) privileges, requiring the user's password.
warnings: sudo commands have full power over the system; double-check before running.
